en: Model inference can be expensive because you
need quite powerful machines with lots of
memory to hold those AI models and to
process incoming requests and produce
responses.
That's why a mechanism called caching is
used to make
them a bit more efficient and to optimize
how that inference process happens. And the
idea in a nutshell simply is
that input
is stored on that server, for example, and
the output, the response that was generated
for it is stored too.
And if you then send a follow-up question,
that stored input and output can be loaded
and doesn't have to be recalculated and just
the updated response needs to be calculated,
which is more efficient.
Now, there is a lot of complexity that goes
into efficient caching, but in a nutshell,
if you hear the term caching, In the context
of these AI models, it's about storing input
and avoiding unnecessary recalculations to
quicker and more cheaply serve updated
responses.
